facts.text: The Historic Cemetery of the Evergreens, founded in 1849, showcases remarkable architecture and art while letting visitors stroll through Glendale’s past.
Glendale’s land was once called Fresh Pond, a swampy area that formed part of a 74,000‑acre expanse known as Newtown.
In 1869 a railroad stop opened at 73rd Street, later becoming part of the Long Island Rail Road’s Montauk Branch.
Forest Park, opened in 1895, was designed under the influence of Frederick Law Olmsted, adding a green landmark to Glendale’s skyline.
Many of Glendale’s homes date to the late 1800s and early 1900s, built in yellow Kreischer brick similar to Ridgewood’s historic buildings.
A bandstand erected in Forest Park in 1898 was followed by a bandshell in 1920, where free concerts ran every weekend until 1995.
